source.title: Generalised André-Pink-Zannier conjecture for Shimura varieties of Abelian type
readSections: The entire published open-access article (§§1–8, Appendices A–B, references), pp.249–331, read 2026-09-22 (PDF from Centre Mersenne, SHA-256 3f3af58def7bb398b3d365ecf828a6571a9477fd7f2b7b891706f146fec05b9e). The companion Comptes Rendus note (10.5802/crmath.751) announces the same result.

summary: Proves the generalised André–Pink–Zannier conjecture for all Shimura varieties of abelian type (Theorem 1.3). More generally, it proves the conjecture for any point satisfying a new uniform integral Tate hypothesis (Theorem 1.4). This extends the conditional result of the authors' earlier Height functions on Hecke orbits. The key new input is polynomial lower bounds for Galois orbits in Hecke orbits (Theorem 5.1). They come from integral and uniform refinements of Faltings' theorems (Theorem 4.7, via Masser–Wüstholz and Noot), Nori theory and Serre's complete reducibility, local relative stability estimates for p-adic norms on closed orbits (Theorem 6.1), and a p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem (Theorem 7.1). The atlas has Shimura varieties, Faltings' isogeny theorem and the Cartan decomposition. It lacks Hecke-orbit heights, the uniform integral Tate hypothesis, p-adic geometric invariant theory over ℤ_p and the André–Pink–Zannier results.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (generalised André–Pink–Zannier)
items.statement: For a Shimura variety S and a subset Σ of a generalised Hecke orbit in S ([40, Def. 2.1]), the irreducible components of the Zariski closure of Σ are weakly special subvarieties.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.1, p.249, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: A case of Zilber–Pink; André 1989, Yafaev 2000, Pink 2005. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Generalised and geometric Hecke orbits (from [40])
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (G, X), x₀ ∈ X with Mumford–Tate group M, φ₀ : M → G the inclusion and W = G·φ₀, points x_φ = x₀∘φ for φ ∈ W(ℚ); the geometric Hecke orbit H^g(x₀), and generalised Hecke orbits, which are finite unions of geometric ones ([40, Def. 2.1, Th. 2.4, Cor. 2.7]).
items.locator: §1, pp.250–251; §3.1, p.255; §4.1, p.256, citing Richard–Yafaev [40], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 ([40, Th. 1.2]: the conditional result)
items.statement: If x₀ ∈ X satisfies the weakly adélic Mumford–Tate conjecture, the conclusion of Conjecture 1.1 holds for every subset of the generalised Hecke orbit of [x₀, 1].
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p.250, citing [40], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: The Pila–Zannier framework, heights on Hecke orbits and the reduction steps that this paper reuses. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (André–Pink–Zannier for Shimura varieties of abelian type)
items.statement: For a point s₀ of a Shimura variety Sh_K(G, X) of abelian type and a subvariety Z whose intersection with the generalised Hecke orbit of s₀ is Zariski dense in Z, Z is a finite union of weakly special subvarieties.
items.locator: Theorem 1.3, p.250, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Theorem 1.4 in the adjoint case via §4.5, and reduction to the adjoint case. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (under the uniform integral Tate conjecture)
items.statement: If s₀ = [x₀, 1] ∈ Sh_K(G, X) and x₀ satisfies the uniform integral Tate conjecture (Definition 2.3), then every subvariety Z whose intersection with the geometric Hecke orbit of s₀ is Zariski dense is a finite union of weakly special subvarieties.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, pp.250–251; proof §3, pp.255–256, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: The proof of [40, §7] with Propositions 4.1–4.5 in the reduction steps and Theorem 5.1 in place of [40, Th. 6.4]. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Definition 2.1 (uniform integral Tate property) and Remarks 2.1.3
items.statement: For reductive M ≤ G over ℚ with integral models from a faithful ρ_G, a compact U ≤ M(𝔸_f) (U_p = M(ℤ_p) ∩ U, U(p) its image in G(𝔽_p), H_p the Zariski closure of U_p) satisfies the uniform integral Tate property if (1) for every p, Z_G(U_p) = Z_G(U_p⁰) = Z_G(M) over ℚ_p and U_p acts semisimply on ℚ_p^d; and (2) for every D there is M(D) such that for p ≥ M(D) and every U′ ≤ U_p of index ≤ D, Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(U′(p)) = Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(M_{𝔽_p}) and U′(p) acts semisimply on 𝔽_p^d. The property is independent of ρ_G, stable under finite-index change (Lemma 2.2) and under intermediate groups.
items.locator: Definition 2.1, Remarks 2.1.3 (1)–(9), Lemma 2.2, pp.252–254, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Nori's theory of subgroups of GL_n(𝔽_p)
items.statement: For p large in terms of n, the subgroup U† of U ≤ GL_n(𝔽_p) generated by unipotent elements is H(𝔽_p)† for an 𝔽_p-algebraic group H (the Nori group); [H(𝔽_p) : H(𝔽_p)†] is bounded in terms of n; semisimplicity of the action corresponds to H reductive ([32], with Serre [46, Th. 5.3]).
items.locator: Remark 2.1.3(1), p.253; §§5.3–5.4, citing Nori [32], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: No atlas layer owns Nori theory. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Definitions 2.3–2.4 (uniform integral Tate conjecture for a point; ℓ-independence)
items.statement: x₀ satisfies the uniform integral Tate conjecture if the image U = ρ_{x₀}(Gal(Ē/E)) ≤ M(𝔸_f) ∩ K of the associated Galois representation ([40, §3.1]) satisfies Definition 2.1; U satisfies ℓ-independence if U = Π_p U_p with U_p ≤ M(ℚ_p).
items.locator: Definitions 2.3–2.4, p.255, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Propositions 4.1–4.3 and 4.5 (functoriality of the hypotheses)
items.statement: The uniform integral Tate conjecture and ℓ-independence pass from x₀ to every point of its geometric Hecke orbit (4.1), to points of a Shimura subdatum (4.2), to images under quotients by central subgroups (4.3), and to the factors of a product of adjoint data (4.5).
items.locator: Propositions 4.1–4.3, 4.5 and proofs, pp.256–259, citing [40, Prop. 3.4] and Serre [46, Th. 5.4], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (misprint E2)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 4.6 (abelian type)
items.statement: Every point of a Shimura variety of abelian and adjoint type satisfies the uniform integral Tate conjecture, and has Galois image satisfying ℓ-independence over some field of finite type.
items.locator: Proposition 4.6 and proof, pp.259–260, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Reduce through (G′, X′) of Hodge type to A_g, then Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.11. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Masser–Wüstholz refinements of the Tate conjecture
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field K and d ≥ 1 there is M′ such that for every prime ℓ > M′ and every open subgroup of the Galois image of index ≤ d·[K:ℚ], 𝔽_ℓ[U′(ℓ)] is semisimple and its commutant in End(A[ℓ]) is End(A/K̄) ⊗ 𝔽_ℓ ([28, Th. 1, Cor. 1, Th. 2]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.7, pp.261–263, citing Masser–Wüstholz [28], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.7 and Proposition 4.8 (uniform integral Faltings over fields of finite type)
items.statement: For A over a field K of finite type over ℚ with End(A/K) = End(A/K̄), Galois image U on T_A ≈ Ẑ^{2dim A} and Z the centraliser of End(A/K) in End_Ẑ(T_A): for every d there is M(A, K, d) such that for every open U′ ≤ U of index ≤ d, Ẑ[U′] ≤ Z is open of index ≤ M(A, K, d); likewise with U replaced by Π_p U_p⁰.
items.locator: Theorem 4.7, Proposition 4.8 and proofs, pp.260–265, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (misprint E1)
items.note: Number fields via Masser–Wüstholz and the double centraliser theorem; general fields by Noot's specialization. Routed to R28.4 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.9 (Serre): ℓ-independence and connectedness of Galois images
items.statement: For A over a number field there is a finite extension L such that the image of Gal(L̄/L) satisfies ℓ-independence (Def. 2.4), has Zariski-connected U_p, and lies in M(Ẑ) for the Mumford–Tate group M ([48, 136 Th. 1; 133; 135 2.2.3], [47, §3.1], [27, 6.14]).
items.locator: Theorem 4.9, pp.263–264, citing Serre [47], [48] and Larsen–Pink [27], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 (Tate modules of abelian varieties) as a source.

items.name: Noot's specialization of abelian varieties over fields of finite type
items.statement: For A over a field K of finite type over ℚ there are a number field F ⊂ K̄ and A_F over F with T_A ≃ T_{A_F}, End(A/K̄) ≃ End(A_F/F) ≃ End(A_F/F̄), and a decomposition subgroup D_F ≤ Gal(K̄/K) with ρ(D_F) = ρ′(Gal(F̄/F)) ([31, §1.2, Cor. 1.5]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.8, pp.264–265, citing Noot [31], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to R01.6 as a source.

items.name: Corollaries 4.10–4.11 (abelian varieties and A_g)
items.statement: The Galois image U ≤ M(Ẑ) of an abelian variety over a field of finite type satisfies the uniform integral Tate property with respect to M and GL(H₁(A; ℚ)), and with respect to GSp(H₁(A; ℚ)); hence every point of A_g satisfies Definition 2.3.
items.locator: Corollaries 4.10–4.11, pp.265–266, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Heights on Hecke orbits and polynomial domination (from [40])
items.statement: The height H_f(φ) = Π_p H_p(φ) on W(𝔸_f), H_p(φ) = max{1, ‖φ(m_{ℤ_p})‖}, the relations ≽ and ≈ of polynomial domination and equivalence ([40, Def. 6.1]), the index bounds [φ(K_M) : φ(K_M) ∩ K] ≈ H_f(φ) ([40, Th. B.1, B.4, C.1, C.2]) and the Lemma of the exponential ([40, Th. A.3]).
items.locator: §§5.1–5.3, citing [40, Def. 6.1, App. A–C], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (polynomial Galois bounds)
items.statement: For connected reductive M ≤ G over ℚ and U ≤ M(𝔸_f) whose image in M^ab is MT and which satisfies the uniform integral Tate conjecture, as φ varies in W(𝔸_f) = (G·φ₀)(𝔸_f): [φ(U) : φ(U) ∩ K] ≈ [φ(K_M) : φ(K_M) ∩ K] ≽ H_f(φ) for every compact open K ≤ G(𝔸_f).
items.note: The core of the paper. Reductions to U = Π U_p with U_p Zariski connected (Theorem B.1, Proposition 5.2), then Theorem 5.4 prime by prime. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 5.3
items.statement: If U satisfies Definition 2.1 with MT abelian image, then Z(M)⁰ ≤ H_p for all p and sup_p #π₀(H_p) < ∞. Lemma 5.3: if n_p ≥ a·h_p^b for all p, where h = Π h_p is the primary factorisation, then Π n_p ≥ α(a,b)·h^{b/2}.
items.locator: Proposition 5.2, pp.267–269; Lemma 5.3, p.270, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 5.4 (local Galois bounds)
items.statement: There are a, c > 0 and b(p) > 0 with b(p) ≥ a for almost all p such that [φ(U_p) : φ(U_p) ∩ K_p] ≥ b(p)·[φ(M(ℤ_p)) : φ(M(ℤ_p)) ∩ K_p]^c for all φ ∈ W(ℚ_p).
items.locator: Theorem 5.4, pp.270–271; proof §§5.2–5.3, pp.271–283, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (misprints E4–E5)
items.note: For each p via closed orbits and functoriality of heights (§5.2). For almost all p via the tuples of Proposition 5.5, Theorem 6.1, the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem and a torus argument (Edixhoven–Yafaev [17, 4.3.9]). Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 5.5 (construction of tuples)
items.statement: For almost all p there are X₁,…,X_k, Y₁,…,Y_l ∈ m_{ℤ_p} with exp(X_i) topologically generating U_p† (the inverse image in U_p of U(p)†), Y_j ∈ ⊕ℤ_pX_i, (1/p)(ℤ_pY₁ + ⋯ + ℤ_pY_l) = z(m)_{ℤ_p} mod p·m_{ℤ_p}, and Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(M_{𝔽_p}) = Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(X̄₁,…,X̄_k, (1/p)Ȳ₁,…,(1/p)Ȳ_l).
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 and proof, pp.273–278, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (misprint E3)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemma 5.6 (closed conjugacy classes and smooth centralisers)
items.statement: For G ≤ GL(n)_{𝔽_p} reductive and v₁,…,v_k ∈ G(𝔽̄_p) generating U acting semisimply on g: if p > 2 dim G then G·v is Zariski closed in G^k; if p > c₃(dim G) the centraliser of v is smooth as a group scheme.
items.locator: Lemma 5.6 and proof, p.278, citing Serre [46], Richardson and Nori [32, Th. E], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 5.7 and Corollary 5.8 (height bounds from tuples)
items.statement: With v = (X, Y) and v′ = (X, Y/p): [φ(U) : φ(U) ∩ G(ℤ_p)] ≥ H_v(φ) ≥ H_{v′}(φ)/p, and H_{v′}(φ) ≥ H_p(φ)^{c(ρ)}; hence if H_{v′}(φ) ∉ {1, p} then [φ(U) : φ(U) ∩ G(ℤ_p)] ≥ H_p(φ)^{c(ρ)/2}.
items.locator: Proposition 5.7, Corollary 5.8, pp.279–280, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (misprint E4)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 5.9, Corollary 5.10, Lemmas 5.11 and 5.13 (structure of the reductions U(p))
items.statement: For almost all p: [Z(M_{𝔽_p})(𝔽_p) : Z(M_{𝔽_p})(𝔽_p) ∩ U(p)] ≤ γ(n)·[M^ab(𝔽_p) : ab(U(p))] ≤ γ(n)·C_MT; the image Û of U(p) in M^ad(𝔽_p) has [Û : Û†] ≤ c(n) (Jordan's theorem, Nori); and an adjoint-group subgroup with Û/Û† abelian, trivial centralisers and semisimple action on bounded-index subgroups has bounded [Û : Û†] (Lemma 5.13).
items.locator: Proposition 5.9, Corollary 5.10, Lemmas 5.11, 5.13 and proofs, pp.283–289, citing Jordan [47, Th. 3′] and Nori [32], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemma 5.12 (adjoint centralisers on a bounded-index subgroup)
items.statement: For every N there is c(N) such that for every prime p, reductive M ≤ GL(N)_{𝔽_p} and U ≤ M(𝔽_p) there is U′ ≤ U of index ≤ c(N) with Z_{M^ad}(ad_M(U′)) = Z_M(U′)/Z(M).
items.locator: Lemma 5.12 and proof, pp.285–287, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) (the proof gives only an inclusion, sourceIssues E6)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemmas 5.14–5.15 (centralisers of large subgroups; bounded fibre components)
items.statement: For connected H ≤ G ≤ GL(d) over ℚ and λ there is N such that for p ≥ N every U ≤ H_{𝔽_p}(𝔽_p) of index ≤ λ has Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(U) = Z_{G_{𝔽_p}}(H_{𝔽_p}) (5.14). For φ : X → Y of finite type over ℤ the number of geometric components of fibres is bounded, and for flat φ the fibre dimension is lower semicontinuous (5.15).
items.locator: Lemmas 5.14–5.15 and proofs, pp.289–290, citing [51, 055H, 0D4H], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Lemma 5.15 is general scheme theory; both are kept here with their only consumer. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemmas 5.16–5.18 and Corollaries 5.17, 5.19 (p-nilpotent lifting and central extensions)
items.statement: A continuous epimorphism of profinite groups lifts topologically p-nilpotent elements to such elements, so φ(U†) = U′† for finite groups (5.16–5.17). If 1 → N → G → H → 1 with #N ≤ n and H abelian, there is an abelian H″ ≤ G with e(n)·h ∈ π(H″) for all h, and [H : π(H″)] ≤ e(#N)^k when H is k-generated (5.18–5.19).
items.locator: Lemmas 5.16, 5.18, Corollaries 5.17, 5.19, pp.290–292, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Goursat's lemma
items.statement: For U ≤ G₁ × G₂ with projections U₁, U₂ and U′₁ = U ∩ (G₁ × 1), U′₂ = U ∩ (1 × G₂), the quotients U₁/U′₁ and U₂/U′₂ are isomorphic.
items.locator: Lemma 5.20, p.292, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Mathlib `Subgroup.goursat` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:128) with `goursatFst`, `goursatSnd`.

items.name: Hyperspecial models, good reduction of tori and the Cartan decomposition
items.statement: For hyperspecial G_{ℤ_p} (special fibre connected reductive), a maximal torus has good reduction with integral weight decomposition ℤ_p^d = ⊕Λ_χ, and G(L) = G_{ℤ_p}(O_L)T_L(L)G_{ℤ_p}(O_L) for a maximally split torus T_L ([52, §§3.3–3.9], [6, 4.4.3]).
items.locator: §6.1, (49)–(52), pp.292–294, citing Tits [52] and Bruhat–Tits [6], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans hyperspecial and parahoric group schemes and RG2.4 the Cartan decomposition in exact generality.

items.name: Theorem 6.1 (local relative stability estimates)
items.statement: For hyperspecial F ≤ G ≤ GL(d) over ℤ_p and non-zero v, v′ ∈ ℤ_p^d whose ℚ_p- and 𝔽_p-orbits are closed with stabilisers F over ℚ_p and F_{𝔽_p} over 𝔽_p (as group schemes), the functions h_v = log max{1, ‖g·v‖} and h_{v′} on G(ℂ_p) satisfy h_v ≤ C h_{v′} and h_{v′} ≤ C h_v with C = C(Σ(ρ)) depending only on the weights of ρ.
items.locator: Theorem 6.1, p.294; proof §6.3, p.295, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Cartan decomposition, the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem and the convexity estimates of §8. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Norms on toric orbits and the apartment (§6.4, Lemma 6.2)
items.statement: For a torus T with good reduction, a_T : T(L) → A_T = Y(T) ⊗ ℝ, h_v = h_µ ∘ a_T with h_µ(a) = max({0} ∪ {ω_χ(a) + µ(χ) : χ ∈ Σ(v)}), and C_µ = {h_µ = 0} is the closure of its rational points (Lemma 6.2).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem)
items.statement: Let F_{ℤ_p} ≤ G_{ℤ_p} ≤ GL(n)_{ℤ_p} be smooth reductive group schemes with G connected, and v ∈ ℤ_p^n with Stab_{G_{ℚ_p}}(v) = F_{ℚ_p}, dim Stab_{G_{𝔽_p}}(v̄) = dim F_{𝔽_p}, and G_{ℚ_p}·v, G_{𝔽_p}·v̄ closed. Then for g ∈ G(ℚ_p), g·v ∈ ℤ_p^n iff f(g) ∈ ℤ_p for all f ∈ ℤ_p[G/F] = ℤ_p[G] ∩ ℚ_p[G]^F; Spec ℤ_p[G/F] is smooth over ℤ_p; and (G(ℚ_p)·v) ∩ ℤ_p^n = G(ℤ_p)·v.
items.locator: Theorem 7.1 and proof, pp.297–299, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: A p-adic analogue of Kempf–Ness in the sense of Burnol's p-adic stability. Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Seshadri's geometric invariant theory over ℤ_p
items.statement: For smooth reductive F ≤ G over ℤ_p, ℤ_p[G]^F is of finite type ([49, §II.4, Th. 2]), and G(k)/F(k) → (G/F)(k) is bijective for every algebraically closed k over ℚ_p or 𝔽_p ([49, §II.1 Prop. 6, §II.3 Prop. 9 Cor. 2]).
items.locator: §7.3.2, Proposition 7.9, (82), pp.305–306, citing Seshadri [49], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition 7.2, Lemmas 7.3–7.4 and Corollary 7.5 (orbit closures over ℤ_p)
items.statement: Every G(ℤ_p)-stable finite-type ℤ_p-subalgebra of ℤ_p[G] is the coordinate ring of an orbit closure of G_{ℚ_p} in some 𝔸^m_{ℤ_p} (7.2); the special fibre of the orbit closure S of v is connected (7.3); if the special orbit of v̄ is closed and stabiliser dimensions agree, (S_{𝔽_p})_red is that orbit (7.4), and stabiliser dimensions over S_{𝔽_p} are bounded by that of v̄ (7.5).
items.locator: Proposition 7.2, Lemmas 7.3–7.4, Corollary 7.5, pp.299–303, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemmas 7.6–7.12 (the quotient G/F over ℤ_p)
items.statement: (G/F)_{𝔽_p} is reduced and ≃ G_{𝔽_p}/F_{𝔽_p} (7.6, via 7.7–7.8); G/F is the normalisation of the orbit closure S (7.10); G → G/F and G/F → Spec ℤ_p are smooth (7.11); orbit maps over a field are flat with dim G·v = dim G − dim Stab_G(v), smooth when the stabiliser is smooth (7.12).
items.locator: Lemmas 7.6–7.8, 7.10–7.12 and proofs, pp.304–310, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Propositions 7.13–7.15 (flatness, integrality and lifting of points)
items.statement: For a closed X ⊆ 𝔸^n over ℤ̄_p of finite presentation, X_red is flat iff X(𝔽̄_p) = r_n(X(ℤ̄_p)) iff the generic fibre is dense iff no component lies in the special fibre (7.13); for flat π : X → Y, y ∈ Y(ℤ̄_p) lifts to X(ℤ̄_p) iff its reduction lifts (7.14); for integral π, x ∈ X(ℚ̄_p) is integral iff π(x) is (7.15).
items.locator: Propositions 7.13–7.15, pp.310–311, citing EGA [14], [15, Prop. 14.5.6], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: General scheme theory. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 8.1, Proposition 8.2 and Corollary 8.3 (slope estimates)
items.statement: For a finite set Σ of linear forms on ℝⁿ and µ : Σ → ℝ_{≤0}, h_µ(x) = max(0, max_λ λ(x) + µ(λ)) satisfies c(Σ) d(C_µ, x) ≤ h_µ(x) ≤ c′(Σ) d(C_µ, x); hence C_µ = C_{µ′} implies h_µ ≤ γ(Σ₀)·h_{µ′} for Σ, Σ′ ⊆ Σ₀.
items.locator: Lemma 8.1, Proposition 8.2, Corollary 8.3, pp.311–314, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Lemmas A.1–A.2, Corollary A.3 (complete reducibility and centralisers)
items.statement: If G′ ≤ H ≤ G ≤ GL(V) over K ≠ 𝔽₂ with V semisimple for G and G′ and equal centralisers, then V is semisimple for H with the same centraliser (A.1). For G-cr H ≤ L ≤ M ≤ G with Z_G(H) = Z_G(M), H, L and M lie in the same parabolics (A.2), and L is G-cr (A.3).
items.locator: Lemmas A.1–A.2, Corollary A.3, pp.314–316, citing Serre [46], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Serre's complete reducibility theory
items.statement: For reductive G over a field, G-complete reducibility of subgroups, the invariant h(G) ≤ dim G, and: for p ≥ h(G) (resp. p > 2h(G) − 2, p ≥ n(Λ)) semisimple representations give G-cr subgroups, G-cr subgroups are strongly reductive in Richardson's sense with closed conjugacy classes of generating tuples ([46, Th. 3.7, Th. 5.3, Th. 5.4, Cor. 5.5]); McNinch: Lie algebras of G-cr subgroups are G-cr and their conjugacy classes closed ([29, Th. 1]).
items.locator: Remark 2.1.3(1), Lemma 5.6, Proposition A.4, citing Serre [46] and McNinch [29], Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Proposition A.4 and Corollary A.5 (closed orbits of Lie algebra tuples)
items.statement: For p ≥ c(M, G) and V ≤ M(𝔽_p) with V ≤ V†·Z(M), Z_G(V) = Z_G(M) and semisimple action, L = W·Z(M) (W the Nori group of V†) and its Lie algebra are G-cr; hence the conjugation orbit of (x₁,…,x_k, y₁,…,y_l) in g^{k+l}, with exp(x_i) generating V† and y_j generating z(m), is Zariski closed.
items.locator: Proposition A.4, Corollary A.5, pp.316–317, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Theorem B.1 and Corollary B.2 (splitting into derived and central parts)
items.statement: If U ≤ M(Ẑ) satisfies Definition 2.1, there is e with u^e ∈ Π_p(U ∩ M^der(ℤ_p))·(U ∩ Z(M)(Ẑ)) for all u ∈ U; if moreover the image W in M^ab satisfies w^f ∈ Π_p W_p, then u^e ∈ Π_p(U ∩ M^der(ℤ_p))·(U ∩ Z(M)(ℤ_p)).
items.locator: Theorem B.1, Corollary B.2, pp.317–318; proof §B.4, pp.324–329, Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier.

items.name: Appendix B lemmas (Tate property over Π𝔽_p, Goursat and Serre's independence criterion)
items.statement: The property Tate(H, C) passes to overgroups (B.4); Γ† = H(𝔽_p)† for a semisimple H with [Γ : Γ†·(Γ ∩ Z(M))] bounded (B.5); for closed W ≤ M(Π𝔽_p), V(p)† ≤ W for p large (B.6); H(𝔽_p)† has no abelian quotient for p ≥ 5 (B.7); simple quotients of subgroups of products come from a factor (B.8); H(𝔽_p)† has no non-trivial map to subquotients of Π GL(n, 𝔽_ℓ), ℓ ≠ p (B.9, after Serre [47]); compact K ≤ GL(n, ℤ_p) with K^e ⊆ L has [K : L] ≤ k(e, n) by the restricted Burnside problem (B.10); Definition 2.1 passes to such V (B.11).

routes.reason: R28.4 owns semisimplicity of Tate modules and Faltings' isogeny theorem. The paper supplies the uniform integral refinement those theorems need here. Using Masser–Wüstholz, Ẑ[U′] has uniformly bounded index in the commutant of End(A) for all open subgroups of bounded index. The paper extends this from number fields to fields of finite type (Theorem 4.7, Proposition 4.8).

R01.6 owns Tate modules of abelian varieties and their Galois representations. The paper uses two inputs about them: Serre's theorems that after a finite extension the ℓ-adic images are independent, Zariski connected and contained in the Mumford–Tate group; and Noot's specialization from fields of finite type to number fields preserving endomorphisms and Tate modules.

SF.0 owns general scheme theory. The criteria for flatness by lifting of points, lifting along flat morphisms, and integrality of points under integral morphisms are general facts that the paper records for use in the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: generalised Hecke orbits and the André–Pink–Zannier conjecture
routes.reason: This is a new direction for Shimura varieties: Hecke-orbit geometry, Galois bounds through integral Tate hypotheses, and p-adic geometric invariant theory. No atlas layer or pending Part II covers it. The existing ShimuraVarieties Part IIs are about integral models, Honda–Tate theory and Kuga–Satake.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.12 and its proof, pp.285–287 (published version)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let m ∈ M(𝔽̄_p) such that m̂ := ad_M(m) belongs to Z_{M^ad}(ad_M(U)). … Since #F | e, by construction of U[e], we have φ_m(U[e]) = {1}. Equivalently m ∈ Z_M(U[e]). This proves the Lemma with U′ = U[e] and c(N) = e^{k(N)}."
sourceIssues.correction: The argument proves the inclusion Z_{M^ad}(ad_M(U)) ⊆ Z_M(U[e])/Z(M). This is what the applications use, and it suffices there. In Lemma 5.11 the Tate hypothesis gives Z_M(V[e]) = Z(M), hence Z_{M^ad}(ad_M(V)) = 1 and so Z_{M^ad}(Û) = 1. Either restate Lemma 5.12 as this inclusion, or supply a separate argument for the equality on U′.
sourceIssues.reason: The lemma asserts Z_{M^ad}(ad_M(U′)) = Z_M(U′)/Z(M) for U′ = U[e]. That needs, for every m with ad_M(m) centralising ad_M(U[e]), that m centralises U[e]. The proof takes m centralising the image of the larger group U. Then φ_m is a homomorphism U → F killed by U[e]. For m only centralising ad_M(U[e]), φ_m is a homomorphism U[e] → F, and U[e] need not lie in its kernel, because homomorphisms of U[e] to F need not extend to U. The inclusion needed for the stated equality is therefore not established.
